idiom_name: class-expression mixins and prototype methods (no static dispatch)
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no static types and no compile-time dispatch: MDN states that 'concepts like static dispatching do not exist in JavaScript', because the prototype chain can be mutated at runtime. The mixin half of CRTP has a direct counterpart - a function taking a base class and returning a subclass (class-expression mixins), or Object.assign copying methods onto a prototype - while the static-polymorphism half is simply unavailable: shared behaviour must accept the receiver at call time (this) and dispatch runs through the prototype chain on every call. Prefer mixins, composition or higher-order functions when the same behaviour must be attached to several classes.
pitfalls: A mixin class expression creates a fresh class per call: applying the same mixin twice in one chain duplicates methods and silently shadows earlier definitions.
Methods copied with Object.assign land as enumerable own properties on the prototype and do not cooperate with super/class semantics; use class expressions when super must work.
Property lookup is dynamic at every call, so nothing checks that a mixed-in class provides the primitive the mixin requires (compare above) - the failure appears at call time, not load time.
alternative: Mixin class-expression factories (Base => class extends Base { ... }) for shared behaviour, Object.assign onto a prototype for simple method copying, and plain closures or composition instead of an inheritance-shaped abstraction; dispatch stays dynamic by design.
